companyName: Fort St. James Green Energy Project

sources.note: Direct retrieval is blocked with HTTP 403. Bing indexes the exact PDF URL and title, with a Fort St. James biomass-project excerpt. The decisive 2013 sponsorship and 2021 BioNorth close claims are independently corroborated by the working direct transaction releases.

The direct 2013 release verifies financial close on November 14, 2013; Fengate Capital Management and Dalkia Canada as developers/equity investors; a C$235 million, 40 MW project; and a 30-year BC Hydro electricity purchase agreement. It does not identify Fengate Infrastructure Fund IV or disclose sponsor percentages.

The filed claim identifies Fort St. James Green Energy Limited Partnership / Société en commandite Fort St. James Énergie Verte and its GP/LP structure, and describes the 40 MW biomass plant. It supports legacy ProjectCo identity, not current ownership.

BioNorth's direct December 2, 2021 release verifies that the acquisition completed, names Arrow, Nak'azdli Development Corporation and Nexus PMG as the JV partners, identifies the 40 MW facility and 30-year EPA, and describes recommissioning. It is the strongest working transaction source.

The British Columbia tenure record shows transfer from Fort St James Green Energy LP to BioNorth Energy LP, describes BioNorth's Arrow/Nak'azdli/Nexus partnership and records approval on February 15, 2022.

BioNorth's FY2026 report verifies continuing 40 MW clean-energy operations, 31 full-time employees and the four current holdco parties. It does not expressly map the two non-Arrow/non-NDC entities to Nexus or disclose their percentages.
Nak'azdli Whut'en's audited financial statements identify BioNorth Holdings Limited Partnership as 40% owned and account for it as a government business enterprise.
Arrow's FY2024 report visually identifies BioNorth Energy Limited Partnership as a 40% joint venture and describes the 40 MW Fort St. James biomass plant.
